newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OECD raises Austria 1996 growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: OECD raises Austria 1996 growth forecast.

text.p: Austria's economy is showing increasing evidence of a slight pickup in growth which should last for two years, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said.

In a semi-annual report, the Paris-based think tank revised its 1996 forecast for real gross domestic product growth up to 1.1 percent from 0.8 percent in June. During 1997, it predicts GDP growth of 1.4 percent.

"Exports, supported by moderate increases in business fixed investment, are projected to underpin growth over the next two years, partially offsetting the temporary effects of sharply reduced public consumption and slow private consumption growth," the OECD report said.
The report was inititally due for release on December 19 but the organisation allowed early release of the report after a European news agency broke the embargo.

Austria has passed austerity budgets for both 1996 and 1997 in a bid to bring its excessive budget deficit down to the three percent of GDP stipulated by the Maastricht criteria for European economic and monetary union.
This effort should continue to keep fiscal policy tight in 1997 as well, the OECD said. But for 1998, it expects the budget deficit to swell back to around 3.5 percent of GDP.
Overall, the OECD sees growth remaining below two percent until 1998, with unemployment likely to increase.
According to OECD standards, Austria's jobless rate stood at 5.9 percent in 1995. This is expected to rise to 6.2 percent this year, and 6.5 percent in 1997.
"However, inflation has fallen by a percentage point since European Union accession and interest rate differentials with Germany are projected to remain very small," the report said.
